issues.title: [feature] Cross-tokenizer teacher distillation (ULD / hybrid), off-policy
issues.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **UPDATE (2026-10-29):** the Gemma 4 byte-offset gap I reported in TRL (huggingface/trl#7995) is fixed by huggingface/trl#8010, merged today. GOLD now aligns byte-fallback BPE tokenizers (Gemma) by bytes, as long as the decoder does not `Strip` the leading space. Llama 2 and Mistral v0.1 still raise.
>
> What changed in this description:
> - **Part A item 3:** the tokenizer gate is now GOLD's own rule (`supports_byte_offsets`): ByteLevel BPE, or byte-fallback BPE without a `Strip` decoder. Before, it was only our coverage check.
> - **Part B step 2:** we port GOLD's offset helpers (`piece_byte_len`, `_normalize_byte_offsets`) instead of writing our own. Added: when rows are encoded in a batch, pad positions are dropped, because Gemma's `tokenizer.json` turns on batch padding (found in the TRL fix).
> - **Considered and rejected, item 2:** GOLD no longer needs positional ULD for Gemma 4.
> - **Question 8:** answered. Gemma 4 no longer waits for TRL, so it lands in the same PR as the ByteLevel pairs. The question is replaced by one about the vocabulary map.
>
> Not changed: the coverage check in Part B step 2 and the byte-matched vocabulary map in Part C step 5 stay Halo-only. TRL's fix did not include them, and GOLD still matches the hybrid vocabulary by raw strings.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue covers **off-policy only**: the same as GOLD with `lmbda = 0`. There is no `lmbda` knob, not even one fixed at 0. Once online OPD with a separate teacher (#38 item 4) lands, we can think about adding `lmbda`. There are two options then: combine off- and on-policy into a single "Distillation" trainer that allows both, or keep the trainers separate and do not allow a random off/on-policy pick per batch, which keeps each trainer clean. The alignment and the loss here are pure functions, so the on-policy path can reuse them either way.

## What & why
Split out of #38, item 3 ("off-policy first; the on-policy version follows once 4 lands").

Let teacher distillation use a teacher whose tokenizer is different from the student's, with the ULD loss and its hybrid variant from TRL's `GOLDTrainer`. Tool-calling datasets must keep working in this mode.

Today:

| Piece | Today | Needed |
|---|---|---|
| Tokenizer check (`shared_vocab_width`, script + trainer) | different token ids → raise | different token ids → cross-tokenizer path |
| Teacher input (`compute_loss`) | the student's `input_ids` | the teacher's own ids for the same text |
| Map (`create_llm_processor`) | student ids | plus teacher ids and the alignment between the two |
| Collator | student ids and labels | plus teacher ids, teacher mask, alignment |
| Loss (`DIVERGENCES`) | per-token divergence over one shared vocab | ULD / hybrid over aligned token groups |
| Tool datasets (`tools_field`) | work: one render, one tokenizer | keep working across tokenizers |

Why it matters:

1. The best teacher is often from another family (for example a Qwen3 teacher for a Llama or LFM2 student). Today the teacher must have the same tokenizer as the student.
2. TRL already has this in `GOLDTrainer` (`use_uld_loss`, `uld_use_hybrid_loss`). Users moving from TRL expect it.
3. Tool datasets. GOLD refuses `tools` together with `use_uld_loss` (my tool-support branch for GOLD, `gold_trainer.py` around L1039). The reason: ULD supports only **one** supervised span per row, and a tool mask cuts holes in it. In Halo the completions-only collator (`src/data/spans.py`) already supervises **every** assistant turn of a row, so even a plain multi-turn chat has several spans. If ULD handles several spans, tool datasets work for free (Part D).

While planning this, I found that GOLD's byte alignment refused Gemma 4 for a reason that was easy to fix: TRL read every token as a ByteLevel piece. Gemma 4 is TRL's own recommended student, so it fell back to positional ULD. I reported it in TRL, and it is now fixed (see the UPDATE at the top).

## Proposed approach

Four parts. A is the gates, B the data path, C the loss, D what it means for multi-turn and tool rows. Same-tokenizer runs keep exactly today's path, including the vocab-padding tolerance from 1.1.0.

### Part A: gates

All checks read only configs and tokenizer files, so every rank reaches the same verdict. The script runs them before any teacher weight loads, and the trainer checks again (the same pattern as `shared_vocab_width` today).

1. **Same token ids** (`require_same_token_ids` passes): today's path, unchanged.
2. **Different token ids:** `distill_loss` must be `uld` or `uld_hybrid`. Any other loss raises and names these two. `kl_divergence` and the rest compare logit rows by token id, which has no meaning across vocabularies.
3. **Both tokenizers must be fast tokenizers that GOLD can align by bytes** (`supports_byte_offsets`): ByteLevel BPE (Llama 3, Qwen, LFM2.5, …), or byte-fallback BPE whose decoder does not `Strip` the leading space (Gemma 4). A `Strip` decoder (Llama 2, Mistral v0.1) and a slow tokenizer raise at startup. On top of that, a row whose byte spans leave a gap in the text raises at map time (the coverage check in Part B step 2).
4. **Refused combinations** (each raises at startup):
   - `apply_hard_labels` and `slim`: both read the teacher's probability at the student's label id, which does not exist across vocabularies;
   - a VLM run: the teacher would need its own processor and its own image-token expansion (a follow-up, question 7);
   - packing / padding-free: each row now has two sequences of different lengths;
   - `tokenizer_backend: gigatoken`: the alignment needs the HF fast tokenizer's offsets.

### Part B: data path (render once, tokenize twice, align at map time)

1. **Render once, with the student's chat template.** `render_conversation` stays as it is, `tools_field` included. The teacher reads the **same text**, the way GOLD does. Both sides then tokenize one string, so their byte offsets share one coordinate system.
2. **Tokenize with both tokenizers.** The student ids come from `tokenize_rendered` exactly as today (a test checks they do not change). The teacher ids come from `tokenize_rendered(teacher_tokenizer, text)`, so each side keeps its own BOS/EOS rules from `probe_tokenizer_specials`. Both calls ask for `return_offsets_mapping=True`.
   - Char offsets become UTF-8 byte offsets. A run of tokens that report the same char span is one multi-byte character split across tokens. The run is split by each token's own bytes: a ByteLevel piece decodes to its bytes, and a byte-fallback token (`<0xF0>`) is exactly one byte. On Gemma 4, an emoji falls back to 4 such tokens with the same char span, and they become 4 one-byte spans.
   - This is GOLD's rule (`piece_byte_len`, `_normalize_byte_offsets`), ported so that Halo and GOLD align the same way.
   - When rows are encoded in a batch, pad positions are dropped: Gemma's `tokenizer.json` turns on batch padding. Halo's per-row `tokenize_rendered` is not affected.
   - Coverage check: after this, the byte spans of all tokens that are not zero-width must be contiguous and cover the rendered text's bytes exactly. A row that fails raises and names the tokenizer. This catches a post-processor with `trim_offsets: true`, which gives whitespace-only tokens zero width, and a normalizer whose offsets no longer map one-to-one to the text. Neither of these can silently drop text from the alignment.
   - Offsets are relative to the one rendered string. A leading BOS that one side strips from the text does not shift the other side.
   - Tokens added by a post-processor (BOS, trailing specials) have zero width. They belong to no group.
3. **Align at map time.** TRL's `_align_by_byte_offsets` walks both offset lists and closes a group wherever both tokenizers have a token boundary at the same byte. It runs over the whole sequence, not only over one completion span. Each row stores:
   - `teacher_input_ids`;
   - `student_group_ids` and `teacher_group_ids`: one group index per token, `-1` for tokens in no group.

   Why at map time: GOLD aligns in Python at every step because on-policy completions change at every step. Off-policy text is fixed, so we pay for the alignment once, and it is cached with the map. The teacher tokenizer's name, revision and a vocab hash go into `cache_key_extras`, so a different teacher never reuses the cache.
4. **Length.** Halo drops over-long rows instead of truncating them, so GOLD's offset rebasing after truncation is not needed. A row is dropped when **either** side is longer than `max_length` (question 5).
5. **Collator.** A thin wrapper around today's text collator (completions-only or padded causal-LM). It pads `teacher_input_ids`, builds `teacher_attention_mask`, and pads both group-id columns with `-1`. The student labels come from today's collator, unchanged.

### Part C: loss

1. **Teacher forward** on `teacher_input_ids` / `teacher_attention_mask` under `torch.no_grad()`, the same frozen, unparallelized teacher as today.
2. **Which groups are trained.** A group is kept only when **every** student token in it is supervised (`labels != -100`). The student labels stay the single source of what is trained. Group edges are byte boundaries shared by both sides, so the teacher side of a kept group covers exactly the same bytes. **The teacher needs no labels and no mask of its own.** A group that crosses the edge of a supervised span is dropped.
3. **Merge a group into one distribution.** For a group of several tokens, use the chain rule in log space (GOLD's `bayesian` strategy): the full distribution at the group's last token, plus the log-probabilities of the actual earlier tokens. Every probability is read at the position that predicts its token (Halo's shifted logits). It is vectorized with gathers and a segment sum over the group ids, in fp32. There is no Python loop over rows or groups (GOLD loops over both).
4. **`uld`:** for each kept group, sort both merged distributions in descending order, pad the shorter vocabulary with zeros, and take the L1 distance. The result is one mean over the kept groups of the micro-batch (the same reduction as `global_token_mean`).
5. **`uld_hybrid`:** a map between the two vocabularies is built once at init as an index tensor. Tokens are matched by the **bytes** they decode to, not by their raw strings. GOLD matches raw strings, which works only between two ByteLevel tokenizers: Qwen writes " hello" as `Ġhello` and Gemma 4 as `▁hello`, so the same text never matches as a string. Byte-fallback tokens (`<0xF0>`) and special tokens are left unmatched. Over the full Gemma 4 ↔ Qwen3 vocabularies, raw strings match 24,519 tokens (160 of them wrongly) and bytes match 95,822.
   - Matched columns: JSD(β) from #95 (`distill_jsd_beta`), on the matched probabilities.
   - Unmatched columns: the sorted L1 from step 4.
   - Weight: `distill_uld_matched_weight`. `None` (the default) is GOLD's adaptive weight, matched count / teacher vocab size; the unmatched term takes `1 − weight`.
6. **Unchanged:** the `distill_alpha` CE term on the student labels and `distill_temperature` (applied to both sides).
7. **New metrics:** `uld_matched_loss` / `uld_unmatched_loss` (hybrid only) and `aligned_token_frac`: the share of supervised student tokens that ended up in a kept group. A low value shows a bad alignment (for example a template the teacher tokenizer splits strangely) without reading the data.

### Part D: multi-turn and tool rows

1. **Why it just works.** Tool results are only more holes in the student labels, next to the user turns. Part C step 2 drops every group that touches a hole. The tool mask works in bytes, not in token ids, so it is the same for both tokenizers.
2. **What is trained.** Exactly what SFT trains on the same row: the assistant turns, tool-call tokens (name and arguments) included. Tool-result tokens are never in the loss when the student's completion spans exclude them, which is what `train_on_completions_only` does with the usual templates.
3. **Known limit: the teacher reads the student's chat template.** The role tokens and the tool-call format (for example Qwen's `<tool_call>` tags) reach the teacher as plain text in a format it was not trained on. Nothing breaks, and GOLD has the same issue for every prompt. But the teacher's targets on tool-call tokens may be weaker. `aligned_token_frac` and the tests below make this visible. Rendering with the teacher's own template is rejected below, and question 6 asks about an option to keep tool calls out of the KD term.
4. **Images in tool results** stay out of scope, as for VLM runs in general (Part A).

### Tests

Every test fails when the behavior breaks. For example, an alignment that drifts by one byte puts a supervised group across a hole, and test 4 catches that.

*CPU (`pytest -m cpu`, no GPU).* They use two tiny ByteLevel BPE tokenizers trained inside the test with different merges, the real Gemma 4 and Qwen3 tokenizers (tokenizer files only; `trl-internal-testing/tiny-Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` is not gated), and the tiny models in `tests/common/tiny_models.py`.

1. Alignment, a pure function: both sides of every group cover the same bytes; zero-width tokens are in no group; a multi-byte UTF-8 character split across tokens differently on each side aligns; identical tokenizers give one-token groups only.
   - Gemma 4: a byte-fallback run (an emoji) splits into one-byte spans, and a Gemma 4 ↔ Qwen3 pair aligns on indented tool-call JSON and non-ASCII text.
   - Coverage check: a tokenizer with trimmed offsets (`trim_offsets: true`) fails it and raises.
2. Map: the student ids equal today's ids exactly; the teacher ids equal the teacher tokenizer's ids for the rendered text; a row over `max_length` on either side is dropped; a different teacher tokenizer misses the map cache.
3. Loss parity with TRL's `ULDLoss` (`bayesian`, extended ULD, hybrid on and off) on single-span rows with fixed seeded logits. If the pinned TRL lacks the byte-offset version, the expected values are produced once from TRL `main` and stored in the test.
4. Multi-span and tools: a row with user → assistant (tool call) → tool result → assistant. Changing the teacher logits at tool-result or user positions does not change the loss. The gradient at those student positions is zero. A group that crosses a span edge is dropped.
5. Identity: the same tokenizer on both sides, forced through the cross-tokenizer path, with teacher logits equal to the student's, gives a loss of 0.
6. Vectorized merge equals GOLD's per-group Python merge on random inputs.
7. Gates: different tokenizers + `kl_divergence` raises and names `uld`; a slow tokenizer raises before teacher weights load; `apply_hard_labels`, `slim`, VLM, packing and `gigatoken` each raise; the same tokenizer keeps today's path.

*GPU (`tests/gpu/manifest.py`, `torchrun`).*

8. Tiny student and teacher with different tokenizers, the student under EP2 and TP2 against one GPU: the same loss and gradients. I have one GPU locally, so this needs your CI or a multi-GPU host.
9. Single-GPU training check: see **Training check** under Scope.

### Considered and rejected

1. **Rendering with the teacher's own chat template.** The two texts then differ (role tokens, tool-call format), so byte offsets no longer share a coordinate system. It would need alignment per message and per content part, a much bigger change. Question 6.
2. **Positional ULD** (cut both sides to the shorter length, like the original ULD paper). It loses the alignment at the first hole, so it is wrong on every multi-turn row. GOLD itself now aligns Gemma 4 by bytes, so no supported tokenizer needs it.
3. **Aligning per step in Python, like GOLD.** The text is fixed offline, so a per-step Python loop is pure overhead.
4. **Teacher labels and a teacher-side tool mask** (what GOLD would need to lift its refusal). Shared byte boundaries make them unnecessary.
5. **Porting the whole `GOLDTrainer`** (`lmbda`, vLLM generation, `seq_kd`). That is on-policy, #38 item 4.
6. **Learned vocabulary projections** (DSKD, X-Token style). They need extra trained parameters. #38 asked for ULD / hybrid.

### Design questions

*Config*

1. **Names:** new `distill_loss` values `uld` and `uld_hybrid` (proposed: one knob, and the gate in Part A reads it), or a separate `cross_tokenizer: bool`?
2. **ULD with the same tokenizer:** refuse it (proposed: KL is exact there, so ULD only loses information), or allow it for ablations?
3. **Merge rule:** only the chain rule (`bayesian`, proposed, because it matches Halo's shifted logits), or expose GOLD's `observed` too?
4. **Hybrid weights:** one knob `distill_uld_matched_weight` with the unmatched term at `1 − w` and `None` = adaptive (proposed), or GOLD's two independent knobs?

*Data*

5. **Length cap:** drop a row when either side is longer than `max_length` (proposed), or cap only the student and check the teacher against its own context window?
6. **Teacher reads the student's template:** fine for v1 (proposed)? Or add a flag that keeps tool-call groups under CE only and out of the KD term?

*Scope*

7. **VLM cross-tokenizer:** a separate follow-up issue (proposed)? GOLD supports it with a second processor for the teacher.
8. **Hybrid vocabulary map:** match tokens by decoded bytes (proposed, Part C step 5), or by raw strings like GOLD? Raw strings are exact between two ByteLevel tokenizers. For a Gemma 4 pair, they find a quarter of the matches, and some of those are wrong.

## Scope & alternatives

**Size (estimate):** ~650 lines of source (alignment ~150, map + collator ~150, loss ~200, gates + config + script ~150) and ~600 lines of tests. One PR, well under 2,000 lines.
**Parallelism:** the student keeps EP, TP, ETP and their combinations, as today. The teacher stays unparallelized, and with replicated `lm_head` the logits on both sides are full-vocab tensors. No collective is added: the group ids are per-row data, and every gate is rank-uniform. CP and PP stay unsupported, as today.
**Sensitive areas:** `src/trainers/distillation/teacher_distillation.py`, so we agree on the approach here before code. Nothing under `src/distributed/`.
**Depends on:** #95 (JSD(β), in review as #106) for the hybrid's matched term.
**Training check (single GPU):** `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct` student from a `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` teacher, the cross-tokenizer pair GOLD recommends (`examples/gold_chatbot_arena/gold_chatbot_arena.py`). Both are Halo families and neither is gated. The runs target one 16 GB GPU, so the student trains with LoRA, using the LoRA settings from GOLD's Gemma 4 example (`lora_r: 64`, `lora_alpha: 16`, `learning_rate: 2e-4`). Other settings: `per_device_train_batch_size: 1` with gradient accumulation to an effective batch of 32 (GOLD's), `max_length: 1024`, gradient checkpointing, a small slice and a fixed `max_steps`.
- Memory (estimate, to confirm on the first run): the bf16 weights take about 10.5 GB (teacher ~8 GB, student ~2.4 GB). The largest temporary tensors are the full-vocab fp32 probabilities that ULD sorts: about 0.6 GB per 1,000 positions for the teacher's 151k vocab, and about as much again for the student's row padded to that width. That is why the batch is 1 and `max_length` is 1024.

Two runs, each shipped as an `examples/distillation/` recipe:
1. **Chat:** `allenai/tulu-3-sft-mixture` (not gated), the dataset of the existing teacher-distillation recipe. It reads the `messages` field with no conversion, and its multi-turn rows train several supervised spans per row.
2. **Tools:** `DataCreatorAI/tool-calling-browser-agent-tasks` (not gated), the dataset of my GOLD tool-calling example (huggingface/trl#6328). This is the run that exercises Part D end to end.
   - It needs a small conversion: keep the conversations that use only the example's six tools, store each conversation as a JSON string (`maybe_parse_json` reads it back, and this avoids Arrow null-padding of the mixed `arguments` structs), and put the tool schemas in a `tools` column for `tools_field`.
   - Unlike the GOLD example, the tool calls stay structured, so each chat template renders them in its own format. The GOLD example writes them inline as Qwen3's `<tool_call>` text, which is wrong for an LFM2.5 student. Whole conversations are kept, not split per user turn.

Both runs check that the loss is finite and falls, and that `aligned_token_frac` stays high. The tools run also checks that tool-result tokens are never supervised. Neither is a direct comparison with GOLD: the chat template and the merge rule differ, so the loss values are not comparable.

**Out of scope:**
- on-policy cross-tokenizer distillation and `lmbda` (see the note at the top);
- VLM cross-tokenizer (question 7);
- chunked loss (#96) and cached teacher targets (#97). A cached cross-tokenizer target would store the teacher's distribution in its own vocab plus the group ids from Part B, so it is a natural follow-up to both;
- self-distillation and SDPG: their teacher is the policy itself, so the tokenizer is the same by construction. The self-distillation reference anchor stays same-tokenizer too.

**Paths:** this issue uses today's `src/` paths. The branch will start from 1.2.0 (`halo/`) once it is out.

## Willing to implement?

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself if it's accepted (a maintainer will comment `/approve @my-handle`)
- [ ] Proposing only — happy for a maintainer or someone else to take it

issues.title: [feature] load native MXFP4 checkpoints (openai/gpt-oss-*) by dequantizing in the lazy loader, not from 3rd party
issues.body:
## What & why

Expert parallelism can't load a natively quantized checkpoint, which rules out the official `openai/gpt-oss-20b` and `-120b` checkpoints. Two checks block them:
- `lazy_load_blocker` (`halo/model_loading/parallel/lazy_plan.py`) refuses any checkpoint that declares a `quantization_config`.
- `apply_ep_layers` (`halo/distributed/expert_parallel/parallelize.py`) then fails fast on any MoE block with non-float expert tensors: "Expert Parallelism requires a de-quantized (BF16) checkpoint".

As a result, the gpt-oss recipes and SkyPilot presets currently point at the third-party `unsloth/gpt-oss-{20b,120b}-BF16` mirrors (`agent-docs/models/gpt-oss.md`, `agent-docs/infrastructure/skypilot.md`).

That would cost users 2 things:
- **A third-party dependency.** Users would need to trust that someone else's re-export matches OpenAI's weights.
- **About 3x the download and disk, when it shouldn't be needed (Halo should handle dequantization of OpenAI's weights instead of them).** MXFP4 expert weights take ~4.25 bits instead of 16. That's ~13 GB vs ~42 GB for 20b, and ~65 GB vs ~234 GB for 120b.

## Proposed approach

Dequantize while loading, inside the EP lazy loader. Each rank decodes only the experts it owns.

- **`lazy_plan.py`:** stop treating `quantization_config.quant_method == "mxfp4"` as a blocker. Every other quantized checkpoint is still refused, with the same reason.
- **`lazy_safetensors/conversion.py`:** add one op to the closed conversion vocabulary.
  - It's a two-source dequantize. It maps `<proj>_blocks` (uint8, two e2m1 codes per byte) plus `<proj>_scales` (uint8 e8m0, bias 127) to the bf16 `<proj>` parameter.
  - It works one expert at a time along dim 0. The planner keeps its ranged reads, and no rank reads another rank's experts.
- **Decoding** follows transformers' `convert_moe_packed_tensors`:
  - The low nibble is the even element. That's the same packing as Halo's `quantize_mxfp4`.
  - Each value is the e2m1 level × 2^(scale − 127).
  - It applies the same transpose to gpt-oss's matmul layout.
  - Every decoded value is exact in bf16, so the output should be bit-identical to transformers' dequantized load.
- **`parallelize.py`** keeps its fail-fast for anything this path doesn't decode.
- **Docs:** `gpt-oss.md` and `skypilot.md` default to `openai/gpt-oss-*`. The BF16 mirror still works.

Tests:
- **CPU, decode:** check the new op against `convert_moe_packed_tensors` on random blocks and on every e8m0 scale code, including both extremes. Make sure they're bit identical.
- **CPU, plan:** build a tiny synthetic gpt-oss checkpoint with `quant_method: "mxfp4"`. Check that the lazy plan maps every `_blocks`/`_scales` key, leaves no checkpoint key unmapped, and still refuses any other `quant_method`.
- **GPU (8× B300, `:blackwell`):** load gpt-oss-20b at EP8 from `openai/gpt-oss-20b`. Compare it with `from_pretrained(..., quantization_config=Mxfp4Config(dequantize=True))`. I'll check:
  - every rank's expert shard is equal;
  - the first-step loss is the same;
  - the peak host RAM per rank during load (reported).

## Scope & alternatives

- **Size:** one op, the blocker change and tests. My estimate is ~200 lines. I'd open the PR after 1.2.0 releases and #115 merges.
- **Alternative: an offline converter** like `convert_glm5_bf16.py`. It is simple, but it keeps the extra step this issue removes, and users still store about 3x the bytes.
- **Out of scope: fp8 releases** (GLM-5, Mistral 4, DeepSeek-V4). They'll keep their offline converters for now. The same op slot could take block-wise fp8 later, reusing `dequantize_block_fp8` from `halo/checkpoint/tools/fp8_dequant.py`, if that's wanted.
- **Weight sync is unchanged.** Training weights are bf16 either way, so on-policy RL keeps serving the BF16 tree, as `gpt-oss.md` already describes.

## Willing to implement?

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself if it's accepted (a maintainer will comment `/approve @my-handle`)
- [ ] Proposing only — happy for a maintainer or someone else to take it

issues.title: Repair published PR-diff tasks after the oracle isolation fix
issues.body:
The generator fix in #145 addresses #144 for new exports. Existing published tasks need a separate migration; changing the library cannot remove files baked into an old task image.

The current manifest for [AdithyaSK/repo2rlenv-pr-diff](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AdithyaSK/repo2rlenv-pr-diff) lists 181 tasks. On 2026-09-22, the sampled [ripgrep task Dockerfile at revision 971b463606b0ffa69ac6b6125d90c6868744be2b](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AdithyaSK/repo2rlenv-pr-diff/blob/971b463606b0ffa69ac6b6125d90c6868744be2b/tasks/BurntSushi__ripgrep-3166/environment/Dockerfile) still embeds `/verifier/oracle.patch` in the agent image. This confirms the published dataset has not been migrated; it is not a claim that all 181 tasks were individually inspected.

Required follow-up:

- Audit all published PR-diff tasks and any copies for baked grading assets.
- Move oracle/verifier assets into `tests/`, update the evaluation script, and clear both reward formats before grading.
- Regenerate hashes/manifests where applicable, rebuild affected images, and invalidate old image caches.
- Check no-op and oracle behavior, and confirm the oracle is absent during the agent phase.
- Publish a new dataset revision with migration notes. Mark old revisions as affected; previous oracle passes do not establish resistance to answer leakage.

Keep this open until the repaired dataset revision and validation evidence are linked here.

issues.title: pr_runtime test.sh: an agent-added conftest.py scores 1.0 with resolved=True
issues.body:
Before grading, the `test.sh` built by `build_eval_script` restores only the files touched by the hidden test patch ([pr_runtime.py#L468-L474](https://github.com/huggingface/Repo2RLEnv/blob/27d04ee8203cd5b2f20c3997d13836e5f5b64238/src/repo2rlenv/pipelines/pr_runtime.py#L468-L474)). Every other file the agent added or changed stays in the working tree, including `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini` and the pytest section of `pyproject.toml`, and pytest loads them during the graded run.

The docstring calls this reset the anti-tamper guard: "the agent CANNOT pass by editing/deleting the tests" ([pr_runtime.py#L452-L454](https://github.com/huggingface/Repo2RLEnv/blob/27d04ee8203cd5b2f20c3997d13836e5f5b64238/src/repo2rlenv/pipelines/pr_runtime.py#L452-L454)). The docs say the same: "The agent can't pass by editing tests" ([pr_runtime.md#L177-L178](https://github.com/huggingface/Repo2RLEnv/blob/27d04ee8203cd5b2f20c3997d13836e5f5b64238/docs/pipelines/pr_runtime.md#L177-L178)). But a test-configuration change alone, with no source fix, can score 1.0 with `resolved=True`.

**Affected (estimate):** this is a static count. 101 of the 219 tasks in the published `FineEnvs/repo2rlenv-pr-runtime`, `FineEnvs/repo2rlenv-commit-runtime` and `FineEnvs/repo2rlenv-cve-patches` datasets run pytest (63 + 19 + 19), so all 101 are probably affected. 9 of them were replayed, and all 9 were affected. The Go tasks don't run pytest. New tasks from `pr_runtime`, `commit_runtime` and `cve_patches` are built by the same function.

`--noconftest` alone wouldn't help, because these repos keep fixtures in their own `tests/conftest.py`. The owned CodeMidas recipe already defaults to it ([recipe_options.py#L178](https://github.com/huggingface/Repo2RLEnv/blob/27d04ee8203cd5b2f20c3997d13836e5f5b64238/src/repo2rlenv/spec/recipe_options.py#L178)).

Fix PR to follow: it restores pytest's configuration to the base commit before the test patch is applied, the same way the test files are restored.

issues.title: Migrate API to FastAPI
issues.body:
The Tornado APi backend should gradually be replaced with FastAPI.
FastAPI is more widely used and has better support for generating OpenAPI specs for automatic API documentation, as well as the possibility to generate TypeScript definitions for the frontend to use.

issues.title: Annotations and Transfer learning
issues.body:
It should be possible to annotate detections directly in the frontend and also perform transfer learning in order to fine tune models.
This is useful to reduce false positives.

issues.title: New Notification domain
issues.body:
A number of components are sending notifications (Gotify, Discord, Telegram).
These all share a lot of similar functionality that is now duplicated across these components.

A new domain, `notification`  should be created for these to inherit from, just like other domains like `object_detector´ etc

issues.title: Using the `useVirtualizer` hook for all frontend pages
issues.body:
When dealing with hundreds or even thousands of items, such as camera data, recordings, or other component data, rendering the page becomes extremely resource-intensive without the `useVirtualizer` hook.

The `useVirtualizer` hook needs to be implemented on any page that renders a large number of data items or cards.

This issue was encountered in https://github.com/roflcoopter/viseron/discussions/1291 and https://github.com/roflcoopter/viseron/discussions/1327.

issues.title: Migrate from custom player to `media-chrome`
issues.body:
The custom player currently implemented for the recording player is difficult to maintain due to the need for numerous callbacks and complex hooks.

This can lead to unpredictable behavior. I propose migrating to the `media-chrome` library, which supports cross-platform native players.

References:
- https://www.media-chrome.org
- https://github.com/muxinc/media-chrome

issues.title: [Bug Report]: 定向邀请每 5 秒拉取完整 visit-hub，持续放大社区请求与推荐计算
issues.body:
## 简短描述

定向邀请的 5 秒兜底轮询调用完整 `GET /api/community/visit-hub`，即使好友面板未打开、没有待处理邀请，也会反复查询关注列表和推荐用户。单页数据下，每次轮询触发 6 次社区上游请求，分页时更多。

本 Issue 专项跟踪 #3568 的 **H-15 / 37-FEA2-02**，补充运行证据、独立 Docker 对照和可兼容修复方案。

## 运行环境与代码位置

- Windows，2026-11-01 本地安装的 Steam Build **26346158**；安装包中的 `visit-chat.js` 与所审查源码一致。
- 源码基线：`f7d274464691cc5fccc3bcf1fae9d82cfa46296e`。
- [邀请轮询实现](https://github.com/Project-N-E-K-O/N.E.K.O/blob/f7d274464691cc5fccc3bcf1fae9d82cfa46296e/static/app/app-react-chat-window/visit-chat.js#L2334)、[500ms 首次检查与 5 秒定时器](https://github.com/Project-N-E-K-O/N.E.K.O/blob/f7d274464691cc5fccc3bcf1fae9d82cfa46296e/static/app/app-react-chat-window/visit-chat.js#L3347)。
- [本地完整社交代理](https://github.com/Project-N-E-K-O/N.E.K.O/blob/f7d274464691cc5fccc3bcf1fae9d82cfa46296e/main_routers/community_remote_proxy.py#L190)、[账号验证入口](https://github.com/Project-N-E-K-O/N.E.K.O/blob/f7d274464691cc5fccc3bcf1fae9d82cfa46296e/main_routers/community_remote_proxy.py#L27)。

## 复现步骤

1. 登录社区，启用串门功能，使用单窗口网页，或 Electron 的 `/chat`、`/chat_full` 窗口。
2. 保持聊天窗口运行，关闭好友面板，不创建邀请。
3. 查看本地请求：启动约 500ms 后开始，每 5 秒请求一次 `/api/community/visit-hub`。
4. 在隔离环境跟踪本地代理的上游调用：身份校验 `/api/users/me`、代理内再次 `/api/users/me`、following、notifications、presence、recommendations，共 6 次；following/notifications 多页时继续增加。

窗口内已有 in-flight 防重入，但它只阻止同一窗口请求重叠，无法减少每轮的全量计算。Pet 多窗口本体不执行这条 UI 轮询；不能将所有窗口都计作轮询源。

## 期望行为

邀请兜底只获取所需邀请状态，并保留身份校验、通知分页、在线心跳、断流恢复和现有 5 秒检查能力。好友面板的完整刷新独立执行。

## 实际行为与影响

邀请处理主要使用 `incoming_invite`、`incoming_invite_ids`、`notifications_ok`，却为此反复构建完整社交数据，包括推荐查询。用户未进行操作也持续产生上游工作。

2026-11-01 12:11:47–12:21:46（UTC+8）的脱敏聚合中，following 第一页共 6,397 次请求；49 个请求目标的中位间隔不超过 10 秒，贡献 5,350 次（83.6%）。这些是 URL 中的目标账号，**不是已认证的唯一调用者、设备或在线人数**；仅凭该日志不能把全部快速请求都归因到此轮询，但源码和隔离复现确认这条放大路径存在。

## 独立 Docker 验证

使用真实本地 Python 代理函数、真实社区业务路由与 PostgreSQL 16 / Redis 7，账号认证为合成夹具；API 为 2 worker、2 CPU。8,000 个合成用户、170 个在线租约，模拟 170 个账号每 60 秒完整刷新，加上 49 个账号每 5 秒邀请检查。每个 20 秒窗口共 253 次轮询，两次镜像顺序重复。

| 条件 | API worker CPU 秒，中位数 | 上游请求/窗口 | 推荐调用/窗口 | 相对原版 CPU 降幅 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 原版 | 8.236 | 1,518 | 253 | — |
| 仅社区服务端优化 | 7.310 | 1,518 | 253 | 11.24% |
| 仅 N.E.K.O 端优化（JS + 本地 Python 代理） | 3.528 | 930 | 57 | 57.17% |
| 两端同时优化 | 3.286 | 930 | 57 | 60.11% |

8 个稳态运行窗口均完成 253 次轮询，失败与推荐降级均为 0。170 个账号的完整社交输出在四组合间一致（排除易变的 `last_seen_at`）；新邀请快照在旧/新社区服务端上均与完整快照一致，共 340 次比较。有效、撤回、过期邀请，以及通知读取失败场景均完成等价检查。

回归：本地代理相关测试 10 passed；真实候选 JS 在 Node 22 Docker 中 4 项行为检查通过，覆盖窗口边界、404/405 兼容、失败保留待处理邀请与权威撤回、单窗口防重入。

**证据边界：**以上是本地合成负载，CPU 只统计 API worker，不含数据库、Redis 和整机 CPU；不是生产容量承诺，也未覆盖真实 Steam/Electron 双账号端到端验收。四组合百分比不可相加。

## 修复候选与验收要求

已在本地准备候选，尚未提交 PR、发布 Steam 更新或部署生产：

- 新增本地 GET `/api/community/visit-invitations`，复用正常身份校验，仅读取完整通知分页与 presence；不再为邀请检查查询额外资料、关注列表和推荐。
- JS 邀请轮询改用精简接口；只有旧本地宿主返回 **404/405** 才回退完整接口，认证、网络及服务端失败不触发全量回退。
- 保留邀请检查频率、SSE、窗口/开关门控及 in-flight；通知读取失败不能错误清除待处理邀请，权威撤回应清除。
- 新 JS 与本地 Python 代理需一起分发。只更新 JS 而宿主仍旧，会兼容回退，无法获得主要减负效果；此方案不要求社区服务端增加新接口。

验收应同时覆盖网页与 Electron 聊天窗口、旧宿主兼容、通知多页和失败语义，并在真实客户端完成邀请接收/撤回/过期/断流恢复测试。

issues.title: Add cgroup v2 job budgets to Linux untrusted runs (3.2)
issues.body:
## Why this needs doing

We’ve put a lot of thought into stopping a hostile PoC from eating the host. There’s still a hole in the resource story: most of our current limits are per process, while a malicious job can fork a whole family of children.

The cgroup namespace we create hides the host’s cgroup path from the payload. Handy, but it doesn’t actually set any resource budgets. And `RLIMIT_AS` stays off by default because it breaks AddressSanitizer workloads. So we can’t currently promise a proper RAM ceiling for the whole job.

For 3.2, let’s add job-wide Linux cgroup v2 limits where the host gives us a delegated, writable cgroup subtree. No pretending a limit is active when it isn’t.

## What to build -- or ponderings on a lazy sunday as i like to think of it. 

- Check that cgroup v2 is mounted, the needed controllers are available, and RAPTOR has a delegated subtree it can safely manage. Don’t require broad privileges to make this work.
- Create a cgroup for each untrusted execution and put the launcher in it before the payload runs, so children inherit the job boundary.
- Apply aggregate memory (`memory.max`), CPU (`cpu.max`) and process-count (`pids.max`) budgets where available. Look at I/O limits too if they’re practical on the supported hosts.
- Make timeout, normal exit, setup failure and parent death clean up the whole job. Surface cleanup failures; don’t just cross our fingers and call it done.
- Record what we asked for, what actually got applied, what the host couldn’t provide and whether cleanup worked. Put this in `sandbox_info` and the run summary.
- If a budget is required but the host can’t enforce it, refuse before the payload starts. If it’s optional, any run on rlimits alone must be an explicit, visible downgrade.
- Keep the existing rlimits as useful inner limits. Don’t turn `RLIMIT_AS` on by default; we still need ASAN to work.

## Done means

1. On a supported delegated cgroup v2 host, memory, CPU and process limits apply to the job as a whole, grandchildren included.
2. After a timeout or teardown, no job processes are left running in the cgroup. If cleanup fails, the caller sees that and the run record says so.
3. Missing delegation or controllers never get reported as an applied limit.
4. ASAN workloads still run when no `RLIMIT_AS` cap was configured.
5. The run record makes it dead obvious whether aggregate limits engaged. A required limit that can’t be applied means the payload doesn’t run.
6. Cover the working path, missing delegation/controllers, descendant limits, timeout and parent-death cleanup, and the reporting/refusal paths.

## Things to settle while designing it

- Which controllers are mandatory for 3.2, and which can be best-effort?
- How do we get a delegated subtree under systemd user sessions and rootless/containerised installs without asking for the keys to the kingdom?
- Are budgets configured per call, in sandbox config, or both? What defaults make sense for builds versus PoCs?
- What’s the exact launch sequence that guarantees the payload can’t fork before it’s in the job cgroup?
- What do we report if the cgroup filesystem disappears or a process gets stuck in uninterruptible sleep?

## Pointers

- `core/sandbox/preexec.py` — current rlimits and teardown
- `core/sandbox/_spawn.py` — Linux namespace launch
- `core/sandbox/tiers.py` — containment floors
- `docs/sandbox.md` — current resource-limit notes
- `sandbox_roadmap.md` — proposed 3.2 scope and wider platform roadmap
- [Linux cgroup v2 docs](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html)

issues.title: CCH rerouting alternates between two stale metrics with cch-update-threshold.factor > 1
issues.body:
Hi,

While looking into @aminissn's question in #18211, I found that CCHMetricFamily keeps the update-threshold state per buffer (myAppliedEffort[2], myPendingList[2], CCHMetricFamily.h:666-668 at 7e5c6a45f09). customize (:344-369) compares an edge's effort with the value the back buffer last applied, and the buffers are published in turn. After a short change, one buffer can keep the new value and the other the old one. Neither updates while the live effort stays within the factor of both, so vehicles routed in alternate adaptation periods use different metrics. On its own it is not a large factor there.

In the attached example (a fork, adaptation every 10 s, one short slowdown), vehicles inserted in alternate 10 s periods take alternate routes until the end. With factor 1 they agree.

Possible fix: one applied effort per edge for both buffers, the back buffer first brought up to the front's arcs. #18400 would only need to save that.

Thanks!

[cch_double_buffer.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33970011/cch_double_buffer.zip)

issues.title: Community project: voice-prefix covers that keep the original melody (yue2-cover)
issues.body:
Hi M-A-P team, thanks for YuE2 and SheetSage2.

I built a small open-source pipeline on top of them and wanted to share it, plus a few things we learned that may help other users: **[yue2-cover](https://github.com/Ornn8/yue2-cover)** re-sings an existing song in a chosen singer's voice over a newly generated arrangement, keeping the song's melody, lyrics and structure.

How it works: SheetSage2 transcribes the song, Whisper word timings place the lyric lines in the score's sections, a 30 s clip of the singer (nearest in tempo) is aligned, encoded to semantic tokens with the community real-audio tokenizer head and forced into YuE2's history, and YuE2 continues over the song's own score (CFG 1.0, NAR 64 steps). No fine-tuning. A 228 s song takes about 230 s on one RTX 3090 (8.5 GB peak).

What made the difference in listening tests:

1. **One tempo for the whole composite score.** When the reference section kept its own `Q:` tempo, the output followed the audio's tempo and turned into speech. We pick the reference clip nearest the song's tempo and stretch it at most 1.18x.
2. **Lyrics in the native section blocks.** One `[Verse]`/`[Chorus]` block per `% label` section, in order, empty blocks for instrumental sections. All lyrics in one block drifted after the first section.
3. **Held line ends.** SheetSage2 often splits a held line-final note into two same-pitch attacks, and YuE2 then sings the last syllable twice. Tying that pair, only in lines with more notes than syllables, fixed it; touching anything else made things worse.
4. **Whisper text.** `condition_on_previous_text` makes long songs loop on one line; Whisper also hallucinates credits and subtitle lines, and stray English over instrumental parts of Chinese songs, which YuE2 then sings. We drop those.
5. **Early stop after the prompt.** Occasionally YuE2 emits the end token right after the forced prefix. It is sensitive to the reference alignment: the same song and clip stopped at 0.9 s with a measured clip tempo of 60.609 BPM and sang the whole song at 60.683 BPM.
6. **Reference length.** MERT drops a sub-second tail for inputs just over a multiple of 30 s, so we avoid those lengths.

The repo includes a tool to build a singer reference library from clips. Happy to hear if any of this is wrong or if there is a better official way to get semantic tokens from real audio.

issues.title: High GC overhead in JIT workload
issues.body:
### Summary

Hi Codon maintainers,

We noticed a performance degradation in a JIT/Python interop workload that appears to be correlated with native GC marking. Codon currently uses the Boehm GC, which is a conservative GC that identifies unreachable objects by tracing pointer chains. Since it cannot precisely distinguish object pointers from pointer-like values, GC collection can become expensive in JIT scenarios where many thread stack frames need to be scanned and marked during `GC_collect_or_expand`.

### Attached traces

I am attaching two Chrome trace JSON files:

- [codon_gc_regression_case_1.trace.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31210931/codon_gc_regression_case_1.trace.json)
- [codon_gc_regression_case_2.trace.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31210944/codon_gc_regression_case_2.trace.json)

They can be opened with Chrome's trace viewer / Perfetto UI.

### Question

- Is this level of GC marking overhead expected for JIT workloads under the current Boehm GC integration?
- Are there recommended ways to reduce this overhead, especially for workloads that create many temporary Codon/Python interop objects or views?

I can try to provide a smaller reproducer if that would be helpful. For now, the attached traces preserve the relevant runtime behavior while removing application-specific details.

Thanks!

issues.title: feat(blender): put unkeyed bones at rest when Apply animation assigns a clip
issues.body:
## Why

Apply animation (#522) copies a returned clip onto the user's own rig. Bones that the clip does not key, such as a static Root above Hips, keep whatever pose the rig already had, so the clip can play from a displaced or rotated pose. On the returned rig those bones are at rest. Review finding: https://github.com/scenario-labs/blender-plugin/pull/522#discussion_r4307048826

## Proposal

When Apply animation assigns the first clip, put the destination bones that exist in the returned rig but are not keyed by any copied clip back to rest (identity location, rotation and scale). Record their previous pose so rollback and Undo restore it exactly. Leave bones that the returned rig does not have untouched.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A posed, unkeyed Root is at rest after Apply animation, and its pose is restored after a failed application and after Undo.
- [ ] Bones absent from the returned rig keep their pose.
- [ ] Installed tests on Blender 5.0, 5.1 and 5.2.

issues.title: ci(tests): track coverage on main and report and gate it in pull requests
issues.body:
## Problem

CI measures unit-test statement coverage on every run (`unit (3.11)` and `unit (3.13)`), but
nothing tracks it: there is no minimum, the reports expire after 14 days, and no pull request
shows how it moved the figure. A drop goes unnoticed unless someone opens the artifact.

The figure also mixes in code the unit suite can never reach. On main (14fb642), the unit run
measures 88.0% of `scenario/core` and `scenario/mcp`:

| Scope | Statements | Covered |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `scenario/core` | 18,386 | 95.9% |
| `scenario/mcp`, without the modules below | 700 | 96.0% |
| `mcp/tools_blender.py`, `mcp/tools_scenario.py` (import `bpy`) | 1,694 | 0% |
| `mcp/stdio_shim.py` (runs as a subprocess) | 43 | 0% |

`scenario/blender`, `scenario/__init__.py` and `scenario/prefs.py` are not measured at all; only
the headless Blender suite exercises them.

## Scope

1. Keep main's coverage for each commit beyond the 14-day artifact and show the trend.
2. On pull requests, report total and changed-line coverage against main in the job summary or
   a comment, fork-safe: read-only token, no secret.
3. Gate regressions: a `fail_under` in `pyproject.toml` just below the baseline, computed
   without the Blender-only modules so it reflects what unit tests can reach, raised as
   coverage grows.
4. Decide whether to measure Blender-side code by running coverage.py inside the headless suite
   (`tools/test_blender.py`) and combining it with the unit data. A separate issue is fine if it
   is large.

Prefer an in-repo approach (main's report kept as the baseline, diffed in pull requests) over an
external service such as Codecov: no account or upload token, and fork pull requests keep
working with a read-only token. Any new tool needs a pinned development dependency.

## Acceptance

- A pull request shows its total and changed-line coverage versus main without opening an
  artifact.
- Main's coverage history is visible beyond 14 days.
- A pull request that drops coverage below the gate fails `ci-ok`.
- `docs/development/validation.md` describes the tracking, the gate and the measured scope.
